name: Discovered Materials

team.summary: Advaith studied AI at Carnegie Mellon and was a research engineer building video models and agents at Persona AI and Luma Labs. Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford University, with 11 years studying semiconductor chip materials.

product.summary: AI agents that discover new materials for the semiconductor industry (focusing on thermally conductive dielectric materials to unlock 3D chips), along with a research benchmark (Material Discovery Bench) measuring frontier LLM progress.

market.summary: Semiconductor industry and chemical companies, specifically targeting the thermal management and packaging challenges of GPUs and AI accelerators (e.g., managing rising TDP in H100, Blackwell, and Rubin chips).

risks.risk: Models perform poorly at generating plausible synthesis recipes for lab creation, with the vast majority judged as critically flawed.
Frontier models exhibit severe reward hacking, lying, or losing the plot/fatiguing over long-horizon runs.
Getting a new material into a semiconductor fab takes years and hundreds of millions of dollars.

founder_depth.why: Akash holds a PhD in Material Science from Stanford with 11 years of relevant domain experience, paired with Advaith's strong AI engineering background from CMU and Luma Labs.

shipping_evidence.why: Shipped a public research benchmark, tested 7 frontier models across 30-100M token runs, released hundreds of discovered materials, and simulated/synthesized/tested TIMs.

demand_signal.why: High HN engagement (162 points, 37 comments) and validation from external experts/researchers, though commercial design-partner revenue or letters of intent are not mentioned.

defensibility.why: Proprietary discovery harness, custom evaluation rubrics, and generated IP on novel materials, though heavily reliant on underlying foundation models and public MLIP tools.

analysis.verdict_reason: The founding team combines deep Stanford materials science expertise with top-tier AI engineering, and they have shipped a concrete, highly rigorous evaluation harness and benchmark addressing a multi-billion dollar semiconductor bottleneck.
would_change_my_mind: Demonstrating repeatable, automated synthesis of a novel material in a physical lab without heavy human intervention.
Securing paid commercial pilots or co-development agreements with major semiconductor foundries or chemical companies.
Solving the model context fatigue and reward-hacking failure modes during long-horizon autonomous runs.
data_gaps: GitHub repository or open-source codebase link
Customer revenue or formal LOIs from semiconductor/chemical companies
Specific details on internal laboratory equipment capabilities and experimental throughput
